code: check_string(x, allow_empty = FALSE) check_bool(x) check_number_whole(x, min = 1, max = 100) check_number_decimal(x) check_character(x, allow_null = TRUE) check_data_frame(x) check_function(x)

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Use cli::cli_abort() call = error_call (call = rlang::caller_env()). Use cli inline markup: {.arg x}, {.cls ClassName}, {.fn function_name}, {.val value}, {.code expr}. S7 validator messages (string returned class validator = function(self) {...}) don’t go cli_abort() since S7 pastes bullets verbatim. Build cli::format_inline() instead sprintf()/paste(), using inline markup, e.g.:
code: cli::format_inline("@value must be one of {.val {self@variants}}")

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Prefer rlang equivalent base R function one exists. particular, use rlang::expr() instead quote() capturing unevaluated expressions (e.g. S7::new_property() promise defaults).

title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: R, use enumerations time, though formally. example, stats::cor()’s argument method = c("pearson", "kendall", "spearman") enumeration method can one three possible values. R, enums typically strings validated via arg.match() equivalent rlang::arg_match(). s7x, enums formalized s7x::Enum class. Note s7x::Enums can cast character vectors. Thus, can use Enum enforce variants, need underlying value can .character() extract ’s value via x@value.
code: library(s7x)  # create a new enum CorMethod <- new_enum("CorMethod", c("pearson", "kendall", "spearman"))  # instantiate the enum x <- CorMethod("pearson") x #> <CorMethod> #>  @ value   : chr "pearson" #>  @ variants: chr [1:3] "pearson" "kendall" "spearman" as.character(x) #> [1] "pearson"

title: Extensions to the S7 Object System
text: longtime wish list item mine scalar properties. scalar R length one vector. useful arguments n_components = 5—wouldn’t make sense value c(5, 1), example. S7 built-classes vector types R (double, integer, character, list) scalar variants. s7x introduces property_scalar() function lets create scalar variants. example: Providing non-length 1 value creates error:
code: library(S7) NComponents := new_class(properties = list(n = property_scalar(class_integer)))  n_comps <- NComponents(5L) n_comps #> <NComponents> #>  @ n: int 5 NComponents(c(5L, 1L)) #> Error in `NComponents()`: #> ! <NComponents> object properties are invalid: #> - @n must be a scalar atomic

title: s7x: Extensions to the 'S7' Object System — s7x-package
text: Provides utilities extend 'S7' object system: enumerated types fixed set variants, scalar-constrained properties, range-bound numeric properties, property-level unions intersections. building blocks make possible express precise, type-safe class properties 'S7' less boilerplate.
